_about: The one filler list. Source of truth: Motherbase shared/fillers.json. SPEAK reads it here; CLIP (tools/fillers.json) and OUTER HEAVEN (jobs/fillers.json) keep byte-identical copies, and a test in each fails when its copy drifts. Edit this file, then copy it over both. Tom's own crutch list in SPEAK (setting speak.crutch) still wins over 'phrases'.
_why: um and uh are their own categories: Clark & Fox Tree 2002 found they behave differently (uh before a short delay, um before a longer one). er and erm are the British spellings of uh and um, so they count under those. Research and sources: Motherbase speak/RESEARCH.md.
